Checks run in layers, each building on the one before:
Checks that the tables and columns delivered match the data dictionary.
Checks that each value can be read as its column's type.
Checks that missing values use the allowed missing-value codes.
Checks that values lie in their column's code list, range, pattern and length.
Checks that keys are present and unique, and link records correctly.
Checks that values agree with each other, and that attributes are given only where they apply.
Error: must be corrected. Warning: should be checked; it may be correct. Flag: unusual but possible. Information: no action needed.

Each issue has a class. Issues for you to act on come from the data as delivered. Issues being fixed in harmonization arise when your data is converted (harmonized), and are fixed there. Issues under review could be either, and are being reviewed.
A missing-value code stands for a value that wasn't measured or doesn't apply. The data dictionary says which codes each column may hold.

Where it can, each issue shows your own key for the record, decoded from the record's ID. Its status says how: decoded; partly decoded; as delivered (your ID, unchanged); record ID only (no decoding was possible); or no key map (no decoding is defined for your data).

A check doesn't evaluate a record when an earlier check failed on the same value: correct the first issue and the later check runs. A record not reached through the keys couldn't be linked to the records a check needs. A check that didn't run gives its reason. None of these counts as a pass.

When a check fails on every record it checked in a column of a dataset, and it checked at least {min_n}, the report shows one issue for the column, with its count, instead of one per record. Checks of a whole column or table, such as a missing column, always show this way.

Tables show at most {row_cap} rows and {example_cap} examples per check, and text longer than {cell_cap} characters is cut and ends with an ellipsis. The issues CSV has every issue, with its text in full.
